The proof in four parts

Sections 2–4 of the paper are proved for an abelian category with a length function; mod Λ and the representations of the linear quiver are instances. Sections 5–8 work with interval representations of the linear quiver. The arguments that differ from the paper are summarized in the proof notes.

Part I: trace and reject

Trace and reject

The trace of a quotient-closed subcategory and the reject of a submodule-closed subcategory, with their properties (Proposition 2.10).

Trace and reject

The trace–reject criterion

A pair of a quotient-closed and a submodule-closed subcategory is a pretorsion theory iff r(X) = r(t(X)) and t(X/r(X)) = t(X)/r(X) for every X (Theorem 2.12).

Theorem 2.12

Torsion pairs

Torsion pairs are the pretorsion theories with zero intersection (Proposition 2.5).

Proposition 2.5

Part II: the lattice of pretorsion theories

Partners

Second components paired with a fixed first component are closed under intersections, proved by dividing by one reject at a time (Proposition 3.2).

Proposition 3.2

The complete lattice

Meets (3.2), joins by duality (3.3), and closure under meets and joins with a fixed intersection (Theorem 3.6, Proposition 3.8).

Theorem 3.6

Part III: image-closed subcategories

Realizations

The greatest and least realizations of an image-closed subcategory, and Theorem A (Theorem 4.4, Corollaries 4.5, 4.7, 4.9).

Theorem A

Convex geometry

Image closure on indecomposable modules is a finitary convex geometry; its extreme points are the splitting projectives and injectives (Theorem 4.11, Proposition 4.13, Corollary 4.14).

Section 4.3

Part IV: counting in type A

Sections 5–8 turn Theorem B into combinatorics of intervals in {1, …, n} and prove the Gandhi recurrences by adjoining one vertex at a time. The Lean development follows this plan; where it differs, the proof notes say how.

Intervals

Every representation is a direct sum of intervals, and image-closed subcategories are the intersection-closed interval families (Theorem 5.5).

Theorem 5.5

Cutoff coordinates

Quotient-closed and submodule-closed subcategories by row and column cutoffs, and the criterion for pretorsion theories (Proposition 6.1, Theorem 6.5).

Theorem 6.5

Weights and column sums

The weight xρq|ind(𝒯 ∩ ℱ)| read off from the cutoffs, and the sums over a new column evaluated by induction: ψ(R) = Δq(x|R|+1) (Lemma 7.3) and θ(R) for image-closed families (8.5).

Column sums

The operator Δq

Δq is characterized by g · (1 + (q − 1)x) = f(1 + qx) − f(x) in ℤ[q][x]; its values on monomials (7.5) and existence give the Gandhi polynomials of both kinds.

Gandhi polynomials

Adjoining a vertex

Restriction to the first vertices, fibre sums and the Gandhi recurrences (Theorems 7.5 and 8.5, Theorem B).

Theorem 7.5
